cards.label: Earlier tonight — Whitechapel
cards.text: Rent is due Friday. The job search has been exhausting and fruitless. You have forty quid left in your account. An old friend, Archie, said he might be able to help. So here you are, behind a chicken shop on Mile End Road at half ten on a Tuesday, while Archie holds a plastic Tesco bag with what looks like an opened Amazon box inside.
The buyers arrive in a grey Vauxhall. Three of them. That's one more than Archie mentioned. He notices too - you can tell by the way he stops whistling.

cards.label: It goes wrong
cards.text: The one nearest to you produces a Stanley knife. His mate grabs the suitcase. The third one just stands there, which is somehow worse. Archie says, very quietly: "Yeah, okay."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Alright chaps?" he lifts the arm with the bag to wave, drawing everyone's eyes. You notice the other hand slip smoothly into his back pocket and pull something small out.

He doesn't even move his arm, just flicks his wrist in a practiced motion and whatever he was holding flies through the air. Only one of the thugs even clocks it, eyes tracing it as it lands harmlessly on the ground between him and his mates. It shatters. The air around the three men goes thick and syrupy. They slow. Not stop - but slow, like a video buffering. Archie wraps the Tesco bag handle around his hand and walks, briskly, to the exit of the alley.

cards.label: Fifteen minutes later — a Wetherspoons
cards.text: Archie orders two pints and a portion of chips. You sit down opposite him. Neither of you say anything until the chips arrive.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Orichalchum. Time-type. Slows things down in a radius - maybe four, five seconds of real time bought, if you compress it right. Was my last one, actually, so cheers for that". He raises his pint to the door, as though saluting the muggers.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Nah". He sips his pint, "Well, almost. It's basically magic. Don't make a big deal out of it. It's just like any product-  some people source it, some people turn it into something useful, some people use it. In between all that, people like us can make a quid or two connecting them. If we're lucky."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Look. You need rent money. I need someone who isn't a liability. Come out with me tomorrow - I've still got the calc from tonight, and I need to move it properly. I'd feel better doing so with backup. You in?"

cards.speaker: You
cards.text: You sigh, thinking about your bank balnace. "Yeah."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Good. I'll text you in the morning. Don't do anything that ends you up in hospital before then."
He finishes his pint and leaves. You sit with the other one and the chips and the fact that your rent problem has, somehow, become a different problem entirely.
